scenes.visual: Portrait pushes in slowly; name and dates appear.

scenes.tts: In February 1828 Wöhler wrote to his old teacher Berzelius with a confession he could not keep to himself.
scenes.visual: Feb 1828 date, Wöhler to Berzelius, letter/confession
scenes.narration: In February 1828 Wöhler wrote to his old teacher Berzelius with a confession he could not keep to himself.

scenes.tts: He had warmed ammonium cyanate, an inorganic salt, and watched it turn into urea — a molecule the body makes to dump nitrogen, identical to the natural product down to the crystal.
scenes.visual: Flask warmed: ammonium cyanate to urea; body dumps nitrogen; identical crystals
scenes.narration: He had warmed ammonium cyanate, an inorganic salt, and watched it turn into urea — a molecule the body makes to dump nitrogen, identical to the natural product down to the crystal.

scenes.tts: He was twenty-seven and understood at once what he held: the same atoms can form different structures, and structure changes everything.
scenes.visual: Twenty-seven; same atoms, different structures; structure changes everything
scenes.narration: He was twenty-seven and understood at once what he held: the same atoms can form different structures, and structure changes everything.

scenes.tts: He never claimed to have conquered the field he opened, calling organic chemistry a primeval forest he had only entered.
scenes.visual: Organic chemistry as a primeval forest; conquered crossed out; only entered
scenes.narration: He never claimed to have conquered the field he opened, calling organic chemistry a primeval forest he had only entered.
